title: Kali’s Propitiation and Banda Singh’s Unfinished Sacrificial Count

blocks.text: The page preserves a grim theological argument in which older ages are invoked to explain the present disaster. Rama had appeased Kali, the Pandavas invoked the goddess in their own age, but in Kaliyuga she devoured them when the rite was not properly completed.

Within that frame Banda Singh instructed the Singhs to understand their suffering as part of an unfinished reckoning rather than a meaningless collapse. The remaining number still had to complete the one lakh and a quarter, a sacrificial count that the page treats as an obligation carried forward into the siege.

This is therefore not simple mythic ornament but a way of interpreting catastrophe. The passage links ancient exemplars, the language of propitiation, and Banda Singh's own exhortation into one continuous appeal for endurance.
